sample_unit: text prompts (33 per model) plus 3 clinical images

links.outcome: Readability (SMOG index) of ChatGPT responses about congenital glaucoma
links.effect: SMOG Index was 14.8 ± 1.2 for ChatGPT-4.0 vs 14.0 ± 1.4 for ChatGPT-3.5 (P = 0.009), indicating college-level reading difficulty.
links.quote: Among readability indices, the SMOG Index score showed more difficult readability scores for ChatGPT-4.0 than for ChatGPT-3.5 (14.8 ± 1.2 vs 14.0 ± 1.4 [P = 0.009]).

links.outcome: Accuracy/appropriateness of clinical content on congenital glaucoma signs and symptoms
links.effect: ChatGPT-4.0 acceptable 22/33 vs ChatGPT-3.5 9/33 (P=0.001); major incorrect information 0/33 vs 6/33 (P=0.02).
links.quote: A higher proportion of prompt responses from ChatGPT-4.0 were graded to be acceptable/appropriate than from ChatGPT-3.5 (22/33 vs 9/33 [P = 0.001]) among text-based queries.

links.outcome: Whether responses raised appropriate concern for congenital glaucoma and potential for harm
links.effect: Appropriate concern raised in 8/11 ChatGPT-4.0 vs 2/11 ChatGPT-3.5 responses (P=0.03); 2 of 3 images had unacceptable responses with high/definitive likelihood of harm.
links.quote: A higher proportion of ChatGPT-4.0 responses were felt to raise appropriate concern for congenital glaucoma (8/11 vs 2/11 [P = 0.03]) and a lower proportion of responses had incorrect or inappropriate information of major clinical significance (0/33 vs 6/33 [P = 0.02]) than ChatGPT-3.5 responses.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the accuracy, appropriateness, readability, and potential harm of ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 on simulated text and image prompts regarding congenital glaucoma without evaluating a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
